interpretability.rationale: Q3: the landing slope limit (2 percent) sets magnitude but not direction, and 'landing or floor' does not say what surfaces make up the landing. Appeal 20-03 turned on both.

ambiguous_terms.issue: Maximum only; direction (toward the door or house) is not addressed.
Undefined; unclear whether a sidewalk plus regraded soil can form the landing.

determinations.citation: SBCTRB Appeal No. 20-03 (Monica and Michael Davis)
determinations.body: Virginia State Building Code Technical Review Board
determinations.binding_effect: Case-specific appeal decision (final order). Shows how the Board applied the text to one dwelling; not a general interpretation.
determinations.holding_summary: Overturned the local findings of no violation for the exterior-door landing and stair landings (owner argued: top landing sloped toward the house, bottom landing sloped toward the handrail and was narrower than the stair; County argued slopes were within 2 percent with normal concrete variation). The decision does not say which argument decided it. Found a garage floor slope violation (R309.1) although the County said the floor sloped toward the door. Upheld no violation of R302.5.2 and of R317.1 (garage door framing not treated as wall framing).

candidate_clarification.note: Consider stating that exterior landings must slope away from the door (within the 2 percent maximum) and that the landing is a single stable surface.
